sources.title: The woolly rhinoceros
sources.author: Museum of Nature and Humankind, University of Padua
sources.location: Species exhibit page and displayed skull photograph
sources.supports: Taxon identification, thick fur, two keratin horns and long anterior horn; skull silhouette and nasal attachment region. No full body is visible in this photograph.
sources.limits: The museum page describes an animal more than two metres tall without a specific measurement basis. Do not use that generalized height in place of primary measured adult proportions.
sources.rights: University of Padua and credited rights holders. Reference image privately consulted only; not incorporated into model, materials or public delivery.

sources.title: Woolly rhino discovery in the lower Kolyma River
sources.author: Boeskorov et al. (2011)
sources.location: Quaternary Science Reviews 30, 2262–2272; Figs 2–3; sections 8.3–8.7; Table 4
sources.supports: Kolyma mummy MM 7938: massive low body, short columnar legs with three hooves, small ears and short thick-based tapering tail. Table 4 provides adult proportion anchors. Fig. 3 supplies curved nasal and shorter frontal horn evidence.
sources.limits: Preserved body is incomplete and distorted, not an exact living surface. Preserved reddish-brown hair may be diagenetically altered. Later 2023 work qualifies interpretation of narrow horn bases.
sources.rights: Elsevier and original authors. Consulted privately from the Rhino Resource Center library copy; no paper figures, photographs or meshes embedded in the public asset.

sources.title: A new discovery in the permafrost of Yakutia sheds light on the nasal horn morphology of the woolly rhinoceros
sources.author: Belyaev, Boeskorov, Cheprasov and Prilepskaya (2023)
sources.location: Journal of Morphology 284, e21626; Fig. 2 and Results; specimen MM 3074
sources.supports: MM 3074 retains a broad oval nasal horn base that matches the skull attachment area, with fore-aft length about 1.5 times transverse width. Constrains the reconstructed attachment, rather than a razor-thin blade base.
sources.limits: The nasal horn was broken during life and worn. Figure 2 constrains the base and skull, not intact horn length or curvature. Authors propose post-burial maceration as the cause of extreme narrowing in many older specimens.
sources.rights: Wiley and original authors. Privately consulted paper and figure raster only. No scientific illustrations or photos incorporated into public model or textures.

reference_use: Scientific facts and visual observation only. All model geometry and material colors are original. References remain outside the public delivery.
